newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds await Spain's ICO, Israel, Slovak water.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds await Spain's ICO, Israel, Slovak water.

text.p: The primary market was caught between a rock and a hard place on Friday following the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday and the weekend which saw new issue activity come to a virtual halt, dealers said.
The focus was thus firmly on the week ahead.

Spain's Istituto de Credito Oficial (ICO) is expected to launch a $500 million five-year Eurobond next week. The proceeds will go to the Spanish Government Development Bank, based in Madrid. The deal is guaranteed by the Kingdom of Spain.
Some traders have said the bond could be launched 18 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Meanwhile Spain is rumoured to be eyeing the mark sector for a jumbo Eurobond issue but syndicate managers said the country should leave the launch until next year.
But the recent poor performance of some mark-denominated offerings meant it was not the best time to issue a bond.
"One thing for sure is that at these levels and at this time of year you have to be much more generous," a trader said.
But Spain -- said to want a payment date before the end of the year, possibly due to its low profile in the international capital market this year -- was anxious to launch a bond, they added.
New issues traders said several banks were bidding for the yet-to-be awarded Spanish mandate.
"Banks are showing Spain several currencies -- dollars, Ecu, marks and sterling," a syndicate manager said.
"Marks seem particularly likely. But we are still in the very early stages. Spain is looking for size, 1.5 to 2.0 billion marks in the five to 10-year sector," another trader said.

At a five-year mark maturity, he said Spain was likely to pay three-month LIBOR flat all-in and at 10 years marginally over LIBOR. "It will depend on what the banks are prepared to show them and how greedy they (Spain) are," he said.
Israel hits London next Wednesday ahead of the launch of a $200 million Eurobond via Merrill Lynch.
It will be the first Eurobond planned for the next three years, during which time Israel expects to raise a total of $750 million.

J.P. Morgan is expected to launch a $200 million 10-year Eurobond for state-owned Slovak water utility Vodohospodarska Vystavba next week. It follows a BBB- rating from Standard & Poor's Corp made on November 27.
